deep.reconstruction:
Context: cote 80 is Grothendieck's c.1981 set of notes on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of pseudolines in the real projective plane, not necessarily simple, studied up to combinatorial isomorphism. This page is written on the back of a 1981 thesis announcement, and the next page is unrelated autobiographical German prose. It states, and partly reworks, a 'Lemme' about building an arrangement up one pseudoline at a time.

Hypothesis. K is an arrangement ('arrangt 1-dimensionnel') of N pseudolines, N ≥ 5, satisfying a non-degeneracy condition involving 'bigonal'. The handwriting gives roughly 'sans ps. droites bigonales'; the machine reading 'pts doubles bigonaux' is doubtful. The term 'bigonal' was presumably defined on earlier pages. From its use here, 'D_i non bigonal dans K_i' seems to describe how the newly added pseudoline D_i sits relative to the previous ones, probably whether its insertion creates or meets 2-gon-like configurations or ordinary crossings.

Conclusion. The pseudolines can be numbered D_1, ..., D_N so that, writing K_i = {D_1, ..., D_i}:
(1) K_4 = D_1, ..., D_4 is of a fixed small type II_4. A marginal correction says that otherwise D_1, ..., D_6 can be taken of type III_6, which is linked to the case 'i ≥ 7'.
(2) For i ≥ 5, D_i is not bigonal in K_i.
A crossed-out NB notes that in some case condition (2) becomes automatic.

Trichotomy. The reworked statement, marked in the margin 'cas mutuellement exclusifs', reads:
(a) Some K_5 is of type II_5. Then, adding pseudolines one at a time, the bigons continue and K is of type II_N, an infinite family indexed by N.
(b) Some K_5 is of type II_{3,2}. Then every further pseudoline is non-bigonal.
(c) K is isomorphic to III_6 or III_7. Then some K_6 is isomorphic to III_6, and in the III_7 case the added seventh line is non-bigonal.
The page ends: 'Le cas de départ est de type II_4 ou III_6.'

The sketch shows 5 lines with two marked triple points that share one line (a vertical line and two others through the left point; the horizontal line and two others through the right point). This is presumably the configuration II_{3,2}: two triple points, sharing a line, among five lines.

Purpose. This is an inductive 'shelling' or construction lemma. Every arrangement in the class is obtained from a small seed (II_4 or III_6) by successively adding pseudolines in a controlled way. Such a lemma would serve to classify, or to prove properties of, arrangements in the class by induction on N. It is in the spirit of Sylvester–Gallai-type and Ringel-type results on removing or adding pseudolines while preserving combinatorial constraints.
errors: The exact definition of 'bigonal' and of the types II_N, II_{3,2}, III_6, III_7 is not on this page, so correctness cannot be fully checked.

The statement is visibly in flux. There are crossed-out fragments ('pour i ≥ 7, D_i ...', 'UPS'), the marginal '(cas i ≥ 7)' qualifier on item 1°, and the statement is then rewritten as a trichotomy. The first formulation (always start with II_4) is apparently corrected to allow a III_6 start.
In case (c) the claim that a III_7 arrangement contains a III_6 sub-arrangement whose complementary line is non-bigonal is asserted without proof on this page.

ideas.what: Inductive ordering of the pseudolines of an arrangement so that the initial sub-arrangements K_i have prescribed small types, and each newly added line satisfies a non-degeneracy ('non bigonal') condition
ideas.modern_name: Incremental construction / extension (shelling-type) lemma for pseudoline arrangements

ideas.what: Trichotomy of arrangements without the forbidden 'bigonal' feature into an infinite family II_N, a family grown from II_{3,2}, and sporadic cases III_6 / III_7
ideas.modern_name: Classification of extremal or special pseudoline arrangements (near-pencil-like families plus sporadic examples)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Comparable classifications appear in Sylvester–Gallai-type literature (Kelly–Moser, Csima–Sawyer, Grünbaum); exact counterpart unsure

missed.claim: A structural classification lemma for a class of (possibly non-simple) pseudoline arrangements. All members arise from seeds II_4 or III_6 by adding lines, with mutually exclusive outcomes: an infinite series II_N, a II_{3,2}-generated series, and sporadic III_6/III_7. Grothendieck's pseudoline notes are largely unstudied, so the precise class and proof are not documented in the literature as his.
missed.quote: ou bien ∃ K_5 de type II_5 ... ou bien ∃ K_5 de type II_{3,2} ... ou bien ∃ K ≃ III_6 ou III_7 ... cas mutuellement exclusifs
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If the class matches a known extremal class (e.g. arrangements with few ordinary points or with restricted cell shapes), this would be an early independent derivation. If it does not, it may be a small classification worth checking against the oriented-matroid / Sylvester–Gallai literature. Value is mainly historical, given the definitions on earlier pages.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working lemma in Grothendieck's little-known 1981 combinatorial notes on pseudoline arrangements. It is interesting as evidence of his post-1970 combinatorial-geometry work and gives a concrete classification sketch. Without the definitions it looks like a routine-to-moderate combinatorial structure lemma in a well-developed field, with no evident deep new idea.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'de N ps. droites, sans ps. droites bigonales, dans N ≥ 5' (or similar) rather than 'sans pts doubles bigonaux'; uncertain.
The marginal insertion on line 1° reads '(cas i ≥ 7)' attached to 'de type II_4', and 'K_i (i ≥ 5)' is an insertion near 'II_5 ... II_N' (the transcription's 'II_i' should probably be 'II_N').
The struck-out text after K_i in 2° ends with a deleted word, and the parenthetical begins 'NB Dans le cas ...'.
Final lines: 'Le cas de départ est de type II_4 ou III_6' ('de telle façon' appears as a struck/handwritten fragment to the right, near the figure).
